definitions.gloss: loss of strength, going limp, relaxing muscles
definitions.explanation: The state of losing physical tension or strength, either intentionally (as in relaxation) or involuntarily (from shock, exhaustion, or disappointment).
A relaxed, understated quality, especially in comedy or creative works.

examples.japanese: {全身|ぜんしん}の{脱力|だつりょく}を{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt all the strength leave my body.

examples.japanese: {肩|かた}の{力|ちから}を{抜|ぬ}いて{脱力|だつりょく}する。
examples.english: To relax the shoulders and go limp.

examples.japanese: {結果|けっか}を{聞|き}いて{脱力|だつりょく}してしまった。
examples.english: When I heard the result, I went limp.

examples.japanese: {脱力|だつりょく}{系|けい}のユーモアだ。
あの{芸人|げいにん}の{脱力|だつりょく}{系|けい}のネタが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like that comedian's deadpan routines.

examples.japanese: {脱力|だつりょく}{感|かん}のあるイラストがSNSで{人気|にんき}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: Loose, relaxed illustrations are gaining popularity on social media.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{脱力|だつりょく}する (to go limp, to lose strength)
・{脱力|だつりょく}{感|かん} (a feeling of limpness/relaxation)
・{脱力|だつりょく}{系|けい} (deadpan style, low-key style)

USAGE:
Sense 1 is used both medically (loss of muscle strength) and casually (going limp from exhaustion, disappointment, or relief). Sense 2 ({脱力|だつりょく}{系|けい}) describes a deliberately understated, relaxed style in comedy, art, or fashion.
